name: capstone
title: The Bounded Observer
author: Daniel John Murray
abstract: We formulate the Universal Hyperbolic Law as an operational framework for bounded normalized readings of positive records. Homogeneity, strong self-duality and a connected equivariant reading–generator correspondence select a simple complex Hermitian matrix algebra. Its elementary binary record has a Lorentz cone, a hyperbolic projective interior and exact rapidity composition under canonical filters. With explicit complex composition and complete positivity premises, records, effects, instruments, purification and environment dilation form a closed operational loop. We prove this closure without demanding that the framework uniquely select every Hamiltonian or constant. A full retained-algebra forgetting law supplies a realizable entropy selector; cumulative dissipative exposure gives a clock-invariant obstruction to finite-resource boundary attainment. We organize exact applications to growth, light, composite records, fields, matter and gravity, identifying the additional physical premises each uses. The singularity hypothesis acquires model-specific regularity and concentration statements. A factorization criterion distinguishes model-dependent preparation readings from claims fixed across physical completions. Historical empirical outcomes and high-scale hypotheses are preserved at their supported strength. The resulting library is mathematically closed as an operational framework with explicit applications, rather than an established derivation of all actual physics from boundedness alone.
keywords: bounded observer; hyperbolic geometry; positive records; operational closure; quantum information; singularities; physical foundations
status: Revised working preprint; no submission performed

name: paper1
title: The Geometry of Bounded Records
author: Daniel John Murray
abstract: We classify finite-dimensional record systems with a proper homogeneous self-dual cone and a linear connected-equivariant bijection between nonconstant readings and reversible generators that conserve their own readings. The cone is a Euclidean Jordan cone by the Koecher–Vinberg theorem. The correspondence excludes direct sums and selects a simple complex Hermitian matrix algebra, apart from the trivial one-dimensional case. Its normalization remains free until a commutator calibration is imposed. For a binary distinction, the positive cone is Lorentzian and its Hilbert projective distance is twice the curvature-minus-one hyperbolic distance. Additive positive readouts give the trace pairing, canonical filters give exact hyperbolic-tangent composition, and two positive filters applied to equilibrium have an order angle determined by their polar rotation. We also derive intrinsic affine record geometry, a spinor pushforward measure, and the covariance-cone form of a specified uncertainty relation. These are closed deductions of the stated operational framework. Their identification with spacetime, physical clocks or particular field dynamics requires separately specified bridges.
status: Revised working preprint; no submission performed

name: paper2
title: One Motion on the Line
author: Daniel John Murray
abstract: A positive two-outcome record has a projective log-odds coordinate. Fixed diagonal filters translate this coordinate and compose the normalized bias by the Einstein addition formula. We show exactly how specified exponential growth, Boltzmann weighting and all-or-none binding models realize this same action. For fixed-rate mixtures, log-odds curvature is the difference of the within-group rate variances, rather than total hidden heterogeneity. We derive the transformation under a variable common clock, establish the finite-atomic criterion for constant-coefficient linear moment closure, and give counterexamples to broader identifiability claims. For an explicitly specified multiplicative Hill benefit–harm response, we prove a necessary and sufficient beneficial-interval condition, its unique peak, its exact amplitude and its threshold asymptotics. This response model is distinct from an additive-rapidity viability model. The results are conditional mathematical laws with experimentally stated model assumptions; boundedness alone does not force exponential growth, a Hill response, a common clock or hormesis. The line construction is self-contained and does not require a quantum or gravitational reconstruction. It supplies a practical common language for several biological models and their falsification.
keywords: log odds; bounded records; selection; hidden heterogeneity; biological clocks; hormesis; Hill response
status: Revised working preprint; no submission performed

name: paper3
title: Light Time and Horizons
author: Daniel John Murray
abstract: A complex binary record has a Lorentz cone and a hyperbolic projective interior. We specify the operational bridges that identify this structure with physical event displacements, null signals and calibrated clocks. The determinant then supplies a conformal Lorentz metric, while a tangent-only Lorentz-invariant clock selects proper time up to scale. Doppler frequencies and normalized binary readouts have a common cone pairing, with different physical calibrations. We prove the distinction among harmonic sky probability, local photon-number density and bolometric radiation moments, give an exact acceleration-horizon criterion, and isolate the Fourier amplitude ratio produced by exponential redshift from the additional quantum assumptions needed for thermality. Positive maps and finite-rank baths yield exact boundary and cumulative-resource inequalities. Within flat scalar wave models, positivity together with sharp retarded support selects three spatial dimensions. The conclusions are closed within their stated operational and physical models; no identification of all qubit operations with frame changes, all radiation with a finite moment state, or all horizons with thermal states is assumed.
status: Revised working preprint; no submission performed

name: paper4
title: Two Observers
author: Daniel John Murray
abstract: We study two complex binary record systems under an explicitly specified tensor-product composition. Local tomography gives sixteen real readings, and the fifteen nonconstant generators contain entangling motions. A pure joint amplitude supplies exact determinant, concurrence, Schmidt and steering identities. Its right purification fiber and left determinant-preserving stabilizer recover the algebraic massive little group, while physical spin and proper time require separate identifications. We construct maximum-entropy forgetting for a complete retained observable algebra, distinguish it from canonical typicality, and prove a clock-invariant full-rank bound for finite-dimensional time-local GKSL evolution. A Busemann barycenter gives a nonlinear projection of angular probability onto harmonic measures, with a finite-entropy condition for its KL interpretation. Independently sampled non-elementary filters have conditional boundary and geodesic-tracking results; isotropic steps yield an exact escape-rate formula. These results close the declared composition and dynamics models without identifying every mixed environment with entanglement, every observer path with a geodesic, or equilibrium state selection with a unique physical generator.
status: Revised working preprint; no submission performed

name: paper5
title: Where Singularities Can Live
author: Daniel John Murray
abstract: A bounded record space supports several inequivalent field geometries and evolution equations. We identify the hypotheses under which its hyperbolic interior and its mixed-qubit hemisphere admit global harmonic-map heat flow. For a fixed closed flat source, hyperbolic heat flow has non-increasing maximum target radius and energy density. A weighted maximum principle proves global regularity for smooth qubit heat-flow data with a strictly positive mixedness margin in the Bures hemisphere. A Bernstein estimate also controls pressure-free self-transport. On two-dimensional sources, sphere-valued heat flow can instead concentrate harmonic spheres; the bubble energy is determined by the normalization of the target metric. We give explicit mixing and attenuation constructions, distinguish their energy and topology statements from claims about arbitrary physical dynamics, and state the precise imported wave-map and equivariant Schrödinger-map results. An optional incompressible Klein-velocity model has a uniquely specified elliptic pressure closure while its global regularity remains conjectural. These results give the singularity hypothesis a conditional mathematical meaning without extending it to all field equations or to spacetime curvature singularities.
keywords: bounded records; harmonic-map heat flow; Bures metric; bubbling; hyperbolic geometry; incompressible flow
status: Revised working preprint; no submission performed

name: paper6
title: The Partner Freedom
author: Daniel John Murray
abstract: Purification supplies a precise freedom of description, but a physical gauge connection requires an additional local frame identification. We formulate that identification explicitly and derive the centred covariance measured by a joint-fidelity experiment. The covariance becomes a trace form on traceless generators at maximal mixing; abelian response requires distinct charge sectors or a relational reference. Given a local Lorentz gauge action and a curvature-quadratic truncation, the leading dynamics is Yang–Mills with independent kinetic coefficients. We then classify Higgs stabilizers, admissible U(2) representations, the faithful local-field Standard Model quotient, and anomaly-free hypercharges within a specified chiral matter and Yukawa family. Right-handed neutrinos leave a B−L mixing freedom rather than forcing an additional gauge field. A conditional minimality theorem selects four completed U(2) doublets of charges (1,1,1,−3). Finally, an electrically neutral CPT pair with specified colour-reference sectors gives a covariance ratio of two. Its interpretation as a coupling relation remains conditional on an operational response-to-action identification. The framework separates mathematical classifications, physical premises and numerical hypotheses.
status: Revised working preprint; no submission performed

name: paper7
title: Gravity as Equilibrium
author: Daniel John Murray
abstract: Hyperbolic geometry enters gravity through two distinct constructions. On a timelike Killing patch, the stationary vacuum Einstein equations reduce to a hyperbolic Ernst map coupled to a three-dimensional quotient metric. We state that reduction, distinguish the stationary ergosurface from the event horizon, and give the precise conditions of an imported smooth-completion theorem. Photon exchange between normalized orbits of the same Killing field has an exact Busemann redshift expression. Separately, area entropy, Unruh temperature, local horizon equilibrium, the all-horizon Clausius relation and stress-tensor conservation imply Einstein's equation by Jacobson's argument. The entropy coefficient and cosmological constant remain physical inputs. Locality and bounded cells alone do not establish the required area entropy. A declared effective-theory non-collapse condition yields a density ceiling; in flat positive-Λ cosmology the future-event-horizon ratio lies below that scale and reaches equality in the de Sitter limit. These are identities and conditional bounds, not a prediction of the vacuum density. We distinguish a possible emergent-metric interpretation from a microscopic quantum-gravity theory and specify the variables, constitutive laws and initial-value requirements needed for a non-equilibrium extension.
keywords: Ernst equation; hyperbolic geometry; local horizon thermodynamics; entanglement entropy; cosmological constant; non-equilibrium gravity
status: Revised working preprint; no submission performed

name: paper8
title: The Ceiling and the Constants
author: Daniel John Murray
abstract: We ask what the bounded-observer framework determines about physical parameters. For fixed constraints and fixed readout operators, the unique finite-dimensional maximum-entropy state defines responses that factor through conserved expectations. We prove the exact rank bound and the Kubo–Mori derivative criterion for preparation-independent readings. A full conserved-algebra conditional expectation supplies an explicit completely positive forgetting semigroup, whereas mean-only Gibbs selection generally cannot be the universal limit of one fixed linear channel. Equilibrium does not determine every dynamical parameter: two locally covariant systems can share the same entropy-maximizing state and conserved algebra while having different clock-independent relative relaxation. Full unitary covariance of dynamics on one carrier is a stronger premise that genuinely selects an isotropic generator. We also classify the complete-positivity cone of the three locally covariant decay rates. We formulate a factorization criterion across admissible physical completions, distinguish preparation data from geometric horizons, and examine the separate cell, criticality and coupling hypotheses. The framework is operationally closed within its stated model class; physical readout, generator and scale identifications remain explicit content. The paper preserves the dated top-mass proposal while correcting its claim to be an already derived precision prediction.
keywords: maximum entropy; conserved observables; quantum channels; physical constants; operational closure; Higgs criticality; bounded observer
status: Revised working preprint; no submission performed

name: hormesis_amendment
title: Exact Onset and Peak Laws for Bounded Adaptive Responses
author: Daniel John Murray
abstract: A published bounded-adaptation model represents repair and damage as opposing rapidity increments, while its analytical approximation multiplies a benefit and a survival factor. These are distinct response models. We derive exact onset, peak and return-to-control conditions for the published additive-rapidity model with equal linear-dose logistic slopes, with an exact zero-dose normalization. Activation before toxicity and greater high-dose damage are not sufficient for a beneficial interval: a further amplitude–slope condition is necessary. We then obtain closed-form laws for an explicitly different log-dose Hill version of the additive model and for the multiplicative Hill response. Their conditions and amplitudes differ, and none has a universal peak at twice the activation threshold. We also derive exact detectable-interval quadratics at a declared assay cutoff. Finally, we distinguish local metabolic-control coefficients from finite enzyme changes and prove an exact finite-gain attenuation law for a specified equal-resistance chain. These results correct the necessity, peak-location and finite-amplitude claims without discarding bounded projective composition. They are analytic model results, not a new fit to biological data. They provide independently testable response laws once their components and matched endpoints are measured.
keywords: hormesis; bounded adaptation; rapidity; dose response; metabolic control; peak location; corrigendum
status: Revised working preprint; no submission performed

name: deformed_kinematics_correction
title: Proposed correction to Bounded Composition and Deformed Kinematics
author: Daniel John Murray
abstract: The composition axioms in the earlier manuscript do not uniquely select Einstein addition or the artanh coordinate. Smooth radial transports of ordinary addition provide explicit counterexamples. The three-dimensional operator appendix also conflates momentum coordinates with boost generators and gives an incorrect radial derivative. The conditional one-dimensional commutator and phase-space measure remain valid when the artanh chart and its canonical quantization are independently specified. We give corrected statements and delimit the physical conclusions that require further dynamics and calibration.
keywords: bounded composition; correction; Einstein addition; momentum coordinates; Snyder algebra
status: Revised working preprint; no submission performed
